title: Finite Tor amplitude and perfectness over the finite coefficient ring
statement:
Let $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ be the
finite coefficient ring,
so that $A$ is a local Artinian ring with maximal ideal
$(\varpi_E)$, and let $C$ be a bounded complex of $A$-modules
whose cohomology modules are finite, i.e. an object of the
finite-coefficient
category over a point of the trace-formula chapter. Then $C$ has
finite Tor amplitude if and
only if $C$ lies in $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ in the sense of
[def-trf-categorical-trace], i.e. if and only if $C$ is
quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated free
$A$-modules.
Here finite Tor amplitude is the ordinary-module condition: there are integers $a\leq b$ such that $H^i(C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M)=0$ for every $A$-module $M$ placed in degree zero and every $i\notin[a,b]$. The notation $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ in the conclusion refers specifically to the perfect category of [def-trf-categorical-trace], rather than to the category of all bounded complexes with finite cohomology.

note: *Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

proof.text: The hypotheses give a finite commutative local ring $A$ with maximal ideal $(\varpi_E)$. Every ideal of $A$ is a finite subset, hence is generated by its elements; thus $A$ is Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Boundedness supplies an integer $b_0$ such that $H^i(C)=0$ for $i>b_0$. The finite cohomology modules are finitely generated as in [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]: if finiteness is read as finiteness of the underlying set, take all their elements as generators. These verifications use no assumption that the terms of $C$ are finite, flat or projective.

source.place: Tag 066E (lemma-Noetherian-pseudo-coherent), clause (2): verification of its hypotheses

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-pseudocoherent-cohomology-criterion] with $R=A$ and $K=C$, using the upper cohomology bound and finite generation established in step 1. Its reverse implication proves that $C$ is pseudo-coherent. In the ordinary-module sense of [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], it therefore admits a bounded-above finite free representative. In particular it admits a bounded-above finite projective representative, since a free module is a direct summand of itself, the projectivity criterion of [def-weil-pbc-projective-module].

source.place: Tag 066E (lemma-Noetherian-pseudo-coherent), clause (2); replaces the insufficient 0-pseudo-coherence inference from Tags 064T and 066B

proof.text: Suppose first that $C$ has finite Tor amplitude. The ordinary-module condition spelled out in the statement is exactly the finite Tor dimension hypothesis of [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-finite-tor-perfect]. Together with step 2, that node gives a bounded complex $E^\bullet$ of finitely generated projective $A$-modules representing $C$. This is precisely membership in the perfect category $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ specified by [def-trf-categorical-trace]. We use only existence of a bounded model from the cited node, not the additional assertion about prescribed amplitude bounds in its source.

source.place: Tag 0658 (lemma-perfect), implication pseudo-coherent + finite Tor dimension => perfect

proof.text: For any object of the perfect category [def-trf-categorical-trace], choose a bounded finite projective representative $E^\bullet$. For each degree $i$, [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat] makes $E^i$ flat. Since $A$ is local and $E^i$ is finitely generated, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free] makes it free. Its basis is finite: finitely many generators involve only a finite union of basis supports, and a basis vector outside that union could not be generated. Choose $e_i:E^i\xrightarrow{\sim}A^{r_i}$, with $r_i=0$ outside a fixed interval supporting $E$. Put $F^i=A^{r_i}$ and $d_F^i=e_{i+1}\circ d_E^i\circ e_i^{-1}$. Then $d_F^{i+1}\circ d_F^i=e_{i+2}\circ d_E^{i+1}\circ d_E^i\circ e_i^{-1}=0$, and the $e_i$ form a chain isomorphism $E^\bullet\cong F^\bullet$. Thus every object of this perfect category, including the object obtained in step 3, has a bounded finite free representative.

source.place: Tag 00NZ (lemma-finite-flat-local); projective => flat as in proof of Tag 051G (lemma-local-artinian-characterize-flat)

proof.text: Conversely, suppose $C$ has a bounded finite free representative $F^\bullet$, supported in integers $[a,b]$ with $a\leq b$. (For the zero complex choose $a=b=0$.) Its terms are flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat]. Its upper degree bound therefore allows [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] to show that it is K-flat, in the ordinary-module sense of [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. For every $A$-module $M$, apply [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model] to $F^\bullet$ and $M[0]$. The isomorphism $Q(F)\cong C$ and this model identify $C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M$ with the complex whose degree $i$ term is $F^i\otimes_A M$. This term is zero outside $[a,b]$, so its cohomology vanishes there. The interval is independent of $M$, proving finite Tor amplitude exactly as defined in the statement. No flatness of $M$ is assumed.

Finally a bounded finite free complex is itself a bounded finite projective complex: each free term is a direct summand of itself, by [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Hence it belongs to the perfect category of [def-trf-categorical-trace]. Step 3 gives finite Tor amplitude $\Rightarrow$ this perfect category, step 4 gives this perfect category $\Rightarrow$ a bounded finite free model, and step 5 gives a bounded finite free model $\Rightarrow$ finite Tor amplitude. These implications prove both equivalences in the statement. No equality between this perfect category and all bounded finite-cohomology objects is claimed.
